name: Materials Compatibility Note 17-B
summary: A buried technical memo warning that a specific class of substitute polymers becomes brittle under Titan-relevant trace contaminants, triggering slow seal failures across Aegis subsystems.

status.practical: unknown (substitution may have resurfaced via procurement waivers)

data.problem_statement: Certain elastomer and polymer seal compounds, acceptable in inner-system habitats, exhibit long-tail brittleness and microcracking when exposed to Titan-relevant trace contaminants and thermal cycling regimes.

failure_signature: increased maintenance frequency without clear root cause
cross-bay correlation that looks like 'bad luck' until it isn't

why_it_got_buried: The approved parts list was updated, and the issue was marked 'resolved.'
Later procurement waivers allowed 'equivalent' substitutes during shortages.
Search terms and tagging were inconsistent; the memo is easy to miss unless you know the exact note number.
story_uses: A technician finds the memo while looking for an unrelated part spec.
A committee insists the risk is already handled, but cannot produce the current substitution list.
A pattern of tiny failures suddenly connects into a single narrative: Compatibility Cascade.
prompt_hooks: Someone references '17-B' like a superstition, but no one can locate it.
A redacted attachment list implies the memo once had stronger language.
A shipment arrives labeled compliant, but the material code matches the memo’s warning.
